questions.question: Identify the pigment that gives blood its colour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haemoglobin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemoglobin **is the pigment responsible for the **red colour of blood**.
 
• It's a **protein** found in **red blood cells**.
 
• **Hemoglobin** carries **oxygen** from the **lungs to body tissues** and returns **carbon dioxide** to the **lungs**.
 
• The **iron-containing heme group** within **haemoglobin** gives blood its r**ed colour**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ferritin**

 
 
• **Ferritin** is a **protein** that **stores iron in cells**.
 
• It helps **regulate iron levels **in **the body**.
 
• Composed of **24 subunits** forming a **spherical structure**.
 
• Measurement of **ferritin levels in blood indicates iron status**.
 
• **Low levels** may indicate** iron deficiency**; **high levels**,** iron overload **or other conditions.
 
 
 
• **Chlorophyll**
 
 
• **Green pigment** found in **chloroplasts** of **plants and algae**.
 
• Essential for **photosynthesis**, converting **sunlight into chemical energ**y.
 
• Absorbs light in **blue and red wavelengths**, **reflecting green light**.
 
• Captures light energy to synthesize **carbohydrates** from **CO2 and water**.
 
• **Molecular structure** includes a **porphyrin ring** with a **magnesium ion**, giving it its **green colour**.
 
 
 
• **Xanthophyll**
 
 
• **Yellow pigment **found in **plants and algae**.
 
• Contributes to **leaf colouration**, **especially in autumn**.
 
• Doesn't directly participate in **photosynthesis**.
 
• Helps dissipate excess **light energy, protecting chlorophyll**.
 
• Also provides **photoprotection against UV radiation.**

questions.question: The liability to pay the tax and the actual burden of which of the following taxes lie on two different persons?

__
 
• It is an **indirect tax** used in India on the supply of goods and services.

 
• It is a **value-added tax** levied on most goods and services sold for domestic consumption.
 
• It was launched in India on **1 July 2017** as a comprehensive indirect tax for the entire country.
 
• It is a comprehensive, multistage, **destination-based tax** comprehensive because it has subsumed almost all the indirect taxes except a few state taxes.
 
• It is paid by the consumers and is remitted to the government by the businesses selling the goods and services.
 
• It is of **three types**__:
 __
 
• **CGST** to be levied by the Centre,
 
• **SGST** to be levied by the States and
 
• **IGST** is a tax levied on all Inter-State supplies of goods and/or services.
 
 
 
• All these taxes are levied at rates mutually agreed upon by the Centre and the States.
 
• The** GST Council** headed by the** Union Finance Minister** is the governing and key decision-making body for GST.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Corporation Tax**__:

 __
 
• Corporation tax is a **tax levied on the profits earned** by domestic companies and foreign companies operating within a country.
 
• It is applicable to the income generated by corporations and is governed by** the Income Tax Act.**
 
• The specific tax rate for corporation tax is prescribed by the government and may change in the annual union budget from time to time.
 
 
 
• **I****nc**ome Tax:__
 __
 
• Income tax is** imposed on the income earned by individuals**. It is one of the most significant sources of revenue for the government.
 
• Individuals pay income tax based on their income brackets. The rates vary depending on the total income and filing status.
 
• The Income Tax Department oversees the collection and administration of income tax in India. You can verify your PAN status, and calculate tax.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Capital Gains Tax:**__

 
 
• 
 
Capital gains tax applies to the **profit or gain arising from the sale of a capital asset.**

 
 
• 
 
There are **two types** of capital gains.

 
 
• **Short-term capital gains (STCG)**: When an asset is held for 36 months or less.
 
 
• STCG tax: Normal slab rates apply when Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is not applicable; 15% when STT is applicable
 
 
 
• **Long-term capital gains (LTCG)**: When an asset is held for more than 36 months.
 
 
• LTCG tax: 10% (for equity shares and units of equity-oriented mutual funds) or 20% (for other assets) on gains exceeding Rs 1 lakh.

questions.question: How many balls are there in an over in cricket?
questions.solution:
correct answer is__** 6.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• There are** 6 balls** in a normal over in cricket.
 
• Each ball must be** bowled by the same bowler**, unless the bowler who starts the over gets injured mid-way through.
 
• An** extra delivery will be added** to the end of the over for each **illegal delivery** that a bowler bowls.
 
 
• Examples of** illegal deliveries are wides and no balls**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the 1800’s at the outset of cricket, overs were 4 balls long.
 
• This then changed to **5 balls in 1889**. 
 
• **1900 came around, the decision was made to change to a 6 ball over**.
 
• Let’s have a look at a few of these below:
 
 
• In** England, 8 ball** overs were trialled briefly in **1939**.
 
• In **Australia, 8 ball **overs were used continuously between **1936 & 1979.**
 
• In** South Africa, 8 ball **overs were used between **1938** and** 1958.**
 
• In** Pakistan, 8 ball overs** were introduced between **1974** and** 1978.**
 
 
 
• **6 ball overs became the international standard in 1979/80 **and those rules have remained in place until this day.

• **​**The **Second Five year Plan** stressed rapid industrialisation and the public sector.

• The budget of the central government and all the state governments is divided into two parts: **non-plan budget and plan budget.**

• The model of the** Indian Economy **was premised on the concept of planning based on five-year plans from **1951-2017.**

questions.question: The agricultural land below the main canal water level forms the ________.

__
 
• **The agricultural land below the main canal water level forms the command area**.
 
• It refers to the region that can be served by a canal system for irrigation purposes.
 
• It refers to the land that receives water from a particular irrigation canal. 
 
• It includes the fields and farms that benefit from the water supply provided by the canal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• 
 
__**Lift System**:__ A lift system involves raising water from a lower level to a higher level using pumps or other mechanisms. While lift systems are relevant for irrigation, they are not directly associated with the agricultural land below the main canal water level.

 
 
• __**Warebandi System :**__ Warebandi is a term used in some regions to describe a rotational system for water distribution among farmers

questions.question: Why do pickles last longer?

options.text: Only beneficial bacteria can grow in the pickle.
The water content of the pickle protect the pickle from spoilage.
Pickle is prepared in a vacuum so that no harmful bacteria can grow on it.
Bacterial and fungal cells get plasmolysed in high salt concentration of pickle.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__** Bacterial and fungal cells get plasmolysed in high salt concentrations of pickle.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pickles **last longer primarily because of the high salt concentration used in their preparation, which causes bacterial and fungal cells to undergo** plasmolysis,** making the environment inhospitable for their growth. 
 
• During the pickling process, beneficial bacteria (such as **lactic acid bacteria**) play a crucial role.
 
• They ferment the sugars present in the vegetables, producing **lactic acid**. 
 
• This acidic environment inhibits the growth of harmful bacteria and preserves the pickle. So, while beneficial bacteria thrive, harmful ones are suppressed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When vegetables are submerged in a brine solution (which contains salt or vinegar), the high salt concentration draws water out of the cells through **osmosis**.
 
• The **reduced water availability prevents the growth of spoilage-causing microorganisms.**
 
• While **vacuum sealing **is used for certain types of pickles, it is not a universal method. 
 
• Vacuum-sealed pickles are prepared in an **environment devoid of oxygen**, preventing the growth of aerobic bacteria and molds.
 
• However, most pickles rely on the natural fermentation process rather than vacuum sealing.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary arylamine in which an amino functional group is substituted for one of the benzene hydrogens?

• Primary arylamines are derivatives of ammonia (**NH**₃) where one hydrogen atom is replaced by an aryl group (a type of aromatic hydrocarbon), directly attached to the nitrogen atom. 
 
• **Quinoline** is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that includes a benzene ring fused to a pyridine ring. It doesn't fit the definition of a primary arylamine because the amino group is not part of its structure.

 
• **Aniline** is the simplest primary arylamine, where the amino group (-NH₂) is directly bonded to a benzene ring. This matches the description provided in the question.

 
• **Pyridine** is a basic heterocyclic aromatic organic compound similar to benzene, with one methine group (=CH−) replaced by a nitrogen atom, but it does not have an amino (-NH2) group attached directly to the ring, so it isn't a primary arylamine.

 
• **Toluidines** include o-toluidine, m-toluidine, and p-toluidine, which are all methyl derivatives of aniline. Like aniline, toluidines are primary arylamines because they have an amino group directly attached to a benzene ring. However, due to the methyl group, they are not the simplest form of primary arylamine, unlike aniline.

questions.question: Which of the following rights was deleted from the list of fundamental rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to property** removed from **fundamental rights **by the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1978.**
 
• Originally part of **Article 19(1)(f) **of **Indian Constitution.**
 
• Reclassified as a **legal right **under **Article 300(A)**.
 
• Aimed at facilitating **land reforms and social welfare policies**.
 
• Increased **state flexibility **in enacting laws related to property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to freedom of religion**

 
 
• The **right to freedom of religion** is enshrined in** Articles 25-28** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 25:- **Guarantees individuals the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• **Article 26:-** Grants religious denominations the right to manage their religious affairs, including establishing religious institutions.
 
• **Article 27:-** Prohibits the state from compelling individuals to pay taxes for promoting or maintaining any particular religion.
 
• **Article 28:-** Ensures that no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained by the state.
 
 
 
• **Right to freedom**
 
 
• The **right to freedom **is enshrined in **Articles 19-22** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 19:-** Guarantees **six freedoms **in India:
 
 
• Freedom of **speech and expression.**
 
• Freedom to **assemble peacefully and without arms**.
 
• Freedom to** form associations or unions**.
 
• Freedom to **move freely throughout India**.
 
• Freedom to **reside and settle in any part of India**.
 
• Freedom to **practice any profession, trade, or business**.
 
 
 
• **Article 20:-** Protects against double jeopardy and self-incrimination.
 
• **Article 21:-** Ensures the right to life and personal liberty.
 
• **Article 22:- **Safeguards individuals against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
 
 
• **Right to equality**
 
 
• The** right to equality** is enshrined in **Articles 14-18** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 14:- **Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to all individuals within the territory of India.
 
• **Article 15:- **Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• **Article 16:- **Ensures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prohibits discrimination in employment on the same grounds as Article 15.
 
• **Article 17:-** Abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18:-** Abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions.
